+# Vector Storage Masterclass
+
+A proposed notebook-based course on building, evaluating, and operating vector retrieval systems, from geometry and exact search to hybrid retrieval, advanced applications, and production operations.
+
+**Status: curriculum design only.** The executable package, Docker Compose services, datasets, tests, and notebooks have not been implemented or validated yet.
+
+The intended stack is Python managed by uv, Jupyter notebooks, Qdrant running in local Docker Compose, and CPU-based embedding inference. The core course should require no paid API or GPU. Real generative-model exercises are an explicit extension, with their dependencies and resource requirements documented separately.
+
+See [the curriculum and implementation blueprint](docs/CURRICULUM.md) for learning outcomes, the proposed notebook sequence, architecture, evaluation strategy, and acceptance criteria.
*** Add File: /Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md
+# Vector Storage Masterclass: curriculum and implementation blueprint
+
+Design date: October 30, 2026. Status: proposed design; no runtime or performance claims have been validated in this workspace.
+
+## Outcome and scope
+
+Teach an AI engineer to select, build, explain, evaluate, and operate a retrieval system. A graduate should be able to justify a design using measured relevance, latency, freshness, cost, and failure behavior, and recognize when vector search is unnecessary.
+
+Use Qdrant as the concrete implementation while teaching transferable information-retrieval and systems concepts. Cover the full lifecycle: source data, representations, indexes, retrieval, downstream applications, evaluation, serving, migration, recovery, and retirement.
+
+“State of the art” is a maintained research track, not a claim that one technique wins every workload. Record paper dates, model revisions, supported server/client versions, and reproducible comparisons. Separate established methods, experimental extensions, and research-only discussion.
+
+Prerequisites: basic Python, HTTP/JSON, SQL familiarity, and basic statistics. Provide a short linear algebra and information-retrieval refresher. No prior vector-database experience required.
+
+Planning estimate: 40–60 hours for the core course including exercises; another 20–40 hours for applications, advanced labs, and the capstone. These are teaching estimates to revise after piloting, not measured completion times.
+
+## Fixed constraints and proposed defaults
+
+- Python and uv, with one project environment, a lockfile, a selected Python version, and an explicitly verified notebook kernel.
+- Qdrant server in local Docker Compose. Use the actual server for integration exercises; embedded/local client mode is not a substitute for server behavior.
+- CPU inference for embeddings, including on Apple Silicon: explicitly select CPU rather than silently using MPS or CUDA. Pin model revisions and record tokenization, prefixes, normalization, dimensions, and precision.
+- Jupyter notebooks for explanations, executable experiments, visualizations, exercises, and interpretations. Shared implementation lives in a small Python package.
+- Default local operation after an explicit initial download of packages, container images, model weights, and datasets. Provide preflight checks for offline availability and artifact licenses/checksums.
+- Select a small dense encoder and small cross-encoder after a CPU pilot. Sentence Transformers is the proposed teaching interface; ONNX/FastEmbed is an optional comparison. Do not silently change models while comparing runtimes.
+- Use NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and modest ipywidgets interaction. Export readable static versions of interactive results.
+- Avoid a mandatory orchestration framework. Teach the retrieval pipeline directly; framework adapters can be optional later.
+- A small versioned filesystem corpus and SQLite ingestion manifest are sufficient initially. Qdrant is a derived search index, with source content and provenance retained separately.
+- Add a small HTTP service, proposed FastAPI, when teaching serving and authorization. Early notebooks use the Qdrant client directly; security exercises use the service boundary.
+- Real LLM generation is an optional explicit dependency. An extractive evidence viewer or recorded fixture must be labeled accordingly and must never be represented as live generative RAG.
+
+The CPU inference track should compare batching, thread counts, sequence lengths, cache behavior, and optional ONNX INT8 inference. Model-weight quantization and stored-vector quantization are separate experiments. Backend changes require quality checks, not just throughput measurements. See [Sentence Transformers efficiency documentation](https://www.sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/usage/efficiency.html). Follow [uv's Jupyter integration guidance](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/jupyter/) for kernel/environment alignment.
+
+## Proposed notebook sequence
+
+Each numbered entry is a focused notebook or, if a pilot reveals excessive length, a small notebook pair. Core notebooks should be independently restartable after documented setup.
+
+| ID | Topic and learning outcome | Experiment or visible evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 00 | Environment, prerequisites, learning map | Verify CPU device, kernel, server version, model cache, and a tiny insert/query round trip. |
+| 01 | Vector geometry | Implement cosine, dot product, and Euclidean distance; visualize normalization and rankings on hand-checkable vectors. |
+| 02 | Embeddings and their limitations | Inspect tokenization, truncation, asymmetric query/document encoding, negation, identifiers, and semantic versus topical similarity. |
+| 03 | Exact retrieval and lexical baselines | Build NumPy exhaustive nearest-neighbor search and a BM25 baseline; show examples where each wins. |
+| 04 | Evaluation before optimization | Create relevance judgments; compute Recall@k, MRR, and nDCG; distinguish ANN recall from relevance recall. |
+| 05 | Qdrant data model and operations | Collections, point IDs, payloads, named vectors, batch writes, retrieval, update, delete, and schema constraints. |
+| 06 | Ingestion as a repeatable data pipeline | Parse source documents; assign stable IDs; retain provenance; retry interrupted batches without duplicates. |
+| 07 | Chunking and context | Compare fixed, structural, parent/child, and contextual chunks; measure truncation, duplication, retrieval quality, and citation fidelity. |
+| 08 | Metadata filters and access boundaries | Compare indexed filters and selectivity; exercise tenant, document-version, and temporal constraints. |
+| 09 | Approximate nearest-neighbor search | Explain HNSW construction and search parameters; compare with exact results at matched filters; plot recall/latency tradeoffs. |
+| 10 | Dense, sparse, and hybrid retrieval | Explain BM25 versus learned sparse representations; compare dense, lexical, sparse, and fusion on the same judgments. |
+| 11 | Reranking and diversity | Add a CPU cross-encoder; vary candidate count; implement MMR and document grouping; inspect gains and regressions. |
+| 12 | RAG foundations | Assemble an evidence/context package with citations and token budgets; optionally run a real generator and evaluate its answers separately. |
+| 13 | RAG failure modes and advanced retrieval | Test query rewriting, decomposition, multi-query retrieval, contextual retrieval, unanswerable questions, contradictory sources, and bounded iterative retrieval. |
+| 14 | Recommendation and discovery | Build content-based item recommendations with exclusions, diversity, freshness, and a temporal evaluation split. |
+| 15 | Deduplication and entity matching | Compare near-duplicate candidate generation with verification; plot threshold precision/recall and false-merge costs. |
+| 16 | Semantic caching and routing | Evaluate false cache hits, context/tenant-sensitive keys, expiration, intent routing, and tool selection with explicit abstention. |
+| 17 | Agent memory | Retrieve episodic records with timestamps and provenance; implement corrections, expiration, deletion, and access tests. |
+| 18 | Classification, clustering, and anomaly triage | Use neighbor voting and density diagnostics; distinguish exploratory visual clusters from validated categories or anomalies. |
+| 19 | Multilingual, code, and multimodal retrieval | Compare suitable encoders on small curated slices; explain shared versus incompatible embedding spaces. |
+| 20 | Storage and CPU efficiency | Measure dimensions, scalar/binary quantization, rescoring, on-disk settings, batch sizes, and total memory/disk cost. |
+| 21 | Matryoshka and multi-stage retrieval | Use a compatible trained model for dimension reduction; compare candidate retrieval and full-resolution rescoring. |
+| 22 | Multi-vector late interaction | Implement MaxSim on hand-checkable matrices, then a small CPU-encoded example using Qdrant multivectors. |
+| 23 | Research extensions | Study visual document retrieval, multi-vector compression, graph-assisted retrieval, and long-context alternatives with small experiments or labeled replay artifacts. |
+| 24 | Serving architecture | Build request validation, timeouts, bounded concurrency, retries, authorization, batching, and tracing around the shared package. |
+| 25 | Index lifecycle and embedding migration | Backfill a new collection, handle concurrent changes, shadow queries, switch aliases, roll back, and validate deletion propagation. |
+| 26 | Performance, observability, and capacity | Run controlled load; separate embedding, search, rerank, and generation time; chart throughput, p50/p95/p99, errors, RAM, and disk. |
+| 27 | Recovery, replication, and failure drills | Verify snapshot restore; use an optional three-node Compose profile to investigate node loss, read consistency, and write behavior. |
+| 28 | Security and adversarial retrieval | Test tenant isolation, malicious payloads, unauthorized documents, prompt injection, poisoning, sensitive logging, and stale permission state. |
+| 29 | Capstone and design review | Deliver an evaluated retrieval service with an architecture decision record, resource budget, migration, recovery evidence, and known limitations. |
+
+The course path is 00–13 followed by 20 and 24–29. Application labs 14–19 and research labs 21–23 branch from it. Instructors can select a shorter introductory path without implying that it covers production operations.
+
+## Advanced coverage and research boundaries
+
+- Hybrid and multi-stage retrieval: candidate generation, rank fusion, reranking, filtering at each stage, and candidate starvation. Qdrant documents dense/sparse combinations, nested prefetch, and fusion; version-gate API use rather than assuming every installed version supports every example. [Qdrant Query API concepts](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/hybrid-queries/)
+- Matryoshka representation learning: variable dimensionality with an appropriately trained model. Arbitrary truncation of an ordinary embedding is not equivalent. [Original research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13147)
+- Late interaction: token-level representations and MaxSim, with explicit storage and compute comparisons. A Qdrant MaxSim demonstration does not reproduce the complete ColBERTv2 training, compression, or serving stack. [ColBERTv2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01488)
+- Contextual retrieval: enrich chunks with document context and measure effects independently of fusion and reranking. Generated context adds ingestion cost and can introduce errors. [Anthropic's method and experiments](https://www.anthropic.com/research/contextual-retrieval)
+- Graph-assisted retrieval: compare relationship traversal and corpus-wide summarization with ordinary retrieval. Qdrant can retrieve vectorized entities or summaries; graph construction/traversal is an additional component, not a native substitute supplied by vector storage. [GraphRAG query modes](https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/query/overview/)
+- Visual document retrieval: study page-image multi-vector representations and the cost of preserving layout. Heavy encoders may require labeled precomputed artifacts for the normal lesson; provide CPU recomputation instructions and realistic resource limits before calling a lab executable. [ColPali](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01449)
+- Multi-vector compression: explain fixed-dimensional encodings, candidate recall, and exact late-interaction rescoring. A pedagogical implementation is not a performance reproduction of the research system. [MUVERA](https://research.google/blog/muvera-making-multi-vector-retrieval-as-fast-as-single-vector-search/)
+- Representation adaptation: teach contrastive objectives, hard negatives, distillation, domain adaptation, and evaluation leakage. A tiny CPU training exercise can demonstrate mechanics; frontier-scale training is outside the local course budget.
+- Cover HNSW versus IVF/PQ, disk-oriented ANN, flat scans, and search-engine/database alternatives conceptually. Clearly label algorithms that are not implemented by the pinned Qdrant configuration.
+- Compare long-context prompting and structured SQL lookups as alternatives for appropriate workloads. Multi-hop or agentic retrieval adds failure paths and needs explicit limits and evidence of benefit.
+
+## Teaching architecture
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    S[Versioned source corpus] --> P[Parse, normalize, chunk]
+    P --> M[Manifest and provenance]
+    P --> E[CPU embedding pipeline]
+    E --> Q[Qdrant in Docker Compose]
+    N[Jupyter lessons and experiments] --> L[Shared Python package]
+    A[Serving API: identity and policy] --> L
+    L --> QE[CPU query encoder]
+    QE --> Q
+    Q --> R[Candidate reranking and context]
+    R --> D[Search, recommendations, memory, cache]
+    R --> G[Optional real generator]
+    L --> V[Evaluation and run artifacts]
+```
+
+The online service derives tenant/access constraints from authenticated context. Users must not be able to remove those constraints through request payloads. Apply restrictions before candidate selection and check authoritative permissions before returning protected content. Test every retrieval branch, reranking input, cache, and fallback path for leakage.
+
+The ingestion manifest records source ID/revision, content hash, parser/chunker versions, model ID/revision, embedding configuration, point IDs, ingestion status, and deletion state. Qdrant does not provide an atomic transaction with the external source store: teach retryable transitions, reconciliation, tombstones, and repair.
+
+A model or chunking migration creates a new explicitly versioned index. Dual writing, an outbox, or replaying a change log must close the gap between backfill and cutover. Switching an alias alone does not establish freshness or synchronization. Include rollback behavior and deletion races in the exercise.
+
+## Data and experiment design
+
+Use a fictional engineering support corpus across the core course: manuals, release notes, troubleshooting tickets, product specifications, and policy documents. Include version conflicts, identifiers, similar products, multiple tenants, obsolete advice, negation, and unanswerable questions. Keep a clear license and no real personal data.
+
+Complement it with a small licensed real-world retrieval benchmark for external validity. Synthetic cases provide controlled failures but cannot establish general retrieval quality. Add small application-specific datasets for recommendations and multimodal work rather than forcing every task into one corpus.
+
+Provide three dataset profiles, with sizes adjusted after the CPU pilot:
+
+- Tiny: hundreds of chunks and hand-checkable relevance judgments for fast demonstrations.
+- Standard: thousands to tens of thousands of chunks for realistic notebook comparisons.
+- Scale: an opt-in larger corpus for index/resource experiments. Generated vectors may illustrate system scaling but must not be used to claim semantic retrieval quality.
+
+Split by source/document family where possible to prevent near-duplicate leakage. Use temporal holdouts for changing catalogs and recommendations. Keep tuning queries separate from a frozen test set. Store query IDs, graded relevance, eligible documents, and annotation rationale; support multiple relevant answers and no-answer queries.
+
+Every run records corpus hash, query/judgment version, git revision when available, model revision, configuration, seed, server/client versions, CPU/OS, Docker resource allocation, warm/cold cache state, timings, and measured outputs. Separate download/setup, embedding, ingestion, indexing, and steady-state query times. Never invent benchmark results or fill missing metrics with illustrative values without an explicit label.
+
+## Testing and acceptance criteria
+
+| Layer | Required evidence |
+| --- | --- |
+| Mathematical and data correctness | Hand-computed distance/ranking cases; metric formulas; stable IDs; chunk boundaries; schema validation; dimension/model mismatch detection. |
+| Real-server integration | Upsert, query, filters, updates, deletes, retries, reruns, aliases, and supported advanced queries against the pinned Compose Qdrant server. |
+| Retrieval quality | Dense and lexical baselines; Recall@k, MRR, nDCG; document versus chunk accounting; slice-level failures; held-out evaluation; uncertainty estimates where sample size permits. |
+| ANN fidelity | Top-k overlap against exhaustive search over the same eligible corpus, same vectors, and same metric; explicit tie handling. Keep this separate from human relevance judgments. |
+| Application correctness | Cache false-hit rate; dedup false merges; recommendation leakage; memory correction/deletion; routing abstention; citations and source versions. |
+| Generative RAG | Answer correctness, citation support, completeness, and abstention assessed separately from retrieval; calibrated human-reviewed examples; no sole reliance on an LLM judge. |
+| Security | Cross-tenant negative tests, forged filters, revoked access, malicious retrieved instructions, cache partitioning, and log redaction. |
+| Performance | End-to-end and stage timing, controlled concurrency, throughput/error rates, sufficient samples for reported percentiles, memory and disk, and cold/warm comparisons. |
+| Operations | Restart persistence, interrupted ingestion recovery, restored-query equivalence, migration rollback, deletion propagation, and node-loss exercises where enabled. |
+| Notebook delivery | Fresh kernel execution, documented prerequisites, no hidden cell order, repeatable reruns, readable static export, and visual review of plots/tables/diagrams. |
+
+Choose thresholds before the capstone evaluation based on the selected hardware and application. Do not hardcode a universal latency or relevance target. Exact fixtures should have exact expected results; real-model comparisons may need tolerances and rank/quality assertions appropriate to platform variation.
+
+Use pytest for shared code and integration tests, and nbclient/nbconvert for notebook execution/export. Keep slow-model, scale, optional-generation, and multi-node checks separately selectable. Local checks are the initial requirement; hosted CI can be added later if requested.
+
+## Notebook teaching contract
+
+Every notebook should include:
+
+1. A concrete engineering question, prerequisites, and learning outcomes.
+2. Intuition, necessary mathematics, and a diagram or hand-worked example.
+3. A small implementation students can inspect before using shared helpers.
+4. A baseline, one controlled change, and measured results.
+5. A visualization that supports the question: rank changes, relevance heatmaps, latency distributions, capacity curves, or failure traces.
+6. A deliberate failure case, troubleshooting guidance, and limitations.
+7. When to use the approach, when to avoid it, and alternatives.
+8. An exercise and a separate worked solution or instructor notes.
+9. Reproducibility metadata, cleanup instructions, and production implications.
+
+Two-dimensional embedding projections illustrate geometry but do not establish retrieval quality. Every interactive widget needs sensible default output for static export. Long preprocessing stages should be explicit and resumable. Lesson reruns must use isolated collection names or narrowly scoped cleanup.
+
+## Production tradeoffs to teach explicitly
+
+Treat relevance, latency, freshness, reliability, operational burden, privacy, and cost as competing objectives. More dimensions, more candidates, larger rerankers, and more retrieval stages require measured justification.
+
+Capacity starts with raw vector bytes, approximately point count × dimensions × bytes per component. Then measure payloads, indexes, multivector counts, replicas, write-ahead logs, snapshots, temporary build space, and page cache. A raw-vector estimate is not a RAM sizing guarantee.
+
+Default Compose should bind published ports to loopback, use persistent volumes, and wait for readiness. Provide explicit destructive-reset commands. Keep API keys out of notebooks and rendered outputs. The security lesson should explain authentication, application authorization, encryption, logging, and network boundaries using [Qdrant security guidance](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/security/).
+
+A three-node cluster on one laptop demonstrates replication mechanics and some failure behavior; it does not prove host, zone, or region resilience. Teach read consistency, write ordering, replication, shard distribution, availability tradeoffs, and reconciliation using the pinned version's semantics. [Distributed deployment documentation](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/scaling/distributed_deployment/)
+
+Backup acceptance means restoring into a clean target and checking configuration, source mappings, and query behavior. A distributed collection snapshot is node-scoped, and collection snapshots do not include collection aliases, so the recovery exercise must account for topology and external metadata. [Qdrant snapshots](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/operations/snapshots/)
+
+Deletion includes the source, all chunk/vector versions, caches, derived artifacts, and defined backup retention behavior. Embeddings should be treated as sensitive derived data, not assumed anonymous.
+
+Production qualification additionally requires representative traffic, real data governance, deployment-specific fault domains, secret management, operational ownership, and application-specific SLOs. The local capstone provides evidence about its tested environment only.
+
+## Proposed repository structure
+
+```text
+compose.yaml                 # one-node default; explicit optional profiles
+pyproject.toml               # uv project and dependency groups
+uv.lock
+notebooks/                   # numbered teaching notebooks
+src/vector_masterclass/      # ingestion, embeddings, retrieval, evaluation, serving
+tests/                       # unit, integration, application, and failure cases
+datasets/                    # licensed small corpus, query sets, judgments, manifests
+configs/                     # reproducible experiment configurations
+scripts/                     # preflight, bootstrap, reset, execute, export, benchmark
+artifacts/                   # generated evidence, with retention/ignore rules
+docs/                        # curriculum, architecture decisions, instructor runbook
+```
+
+This tree is a proposal; only the curriculum and README currently exist.
+
+## Implementation sequence and decision gates
+
+1. Build one vertical slice: uv/Jupyter, pinned Compose Qdrant, CPU encoder, tiny corpus, exact and lexical baselines, retrieval metrics, and the first few lessons. Validate install, rerun, export, and plot readability.
+2. Complete the core retrieval path through ingestion, filters, ANN, hybrid retrieval, reranking, and evidence assembly. Require shared held-out comparisons before adding complexity.
+3. Add non-RAG application labs with their own task metrics and negative cases.
+4. Add serving, security, lifecycle, migration, observability, and recovery, using the same tested implementation from the notebooks.
+5. Add advanced CPU experiments and clearly labeled research/replay extensions. Select exact models and methods based on measured feasibility rather than paper prominence.
+6. Pilot the course, revise runtime estimates, and finish the capstone, instructor runbook, and reproducible artifacts.
+
+Before implementing optional generation, select a real local CPU model/backend or an explicitly configured hosted model. The default course can teach retrieval and context construction without a generator, but live generative-RAG lessons require one. Keep any precomputed model outputs visibly identified throughout the notebooks and reports.
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
Yes. I’d design this as **a masterclass in building and operating retrieval systems**, with vector storage as the foundation. Students should finish able to explain *why* a design works, measure its quality, and manage its failure modes.

I’ve saved a concrete [curriculum and implementation blueprint](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md) and a [project README](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/README.md). These are design documents; the notebooks and runtime have not been implemented yet.

Your chosen stack is a good fit:

- **Qdrant in local Docker Compose** for the actual database exercises.
- **Python and uv** for a reproducible environment.
- **CPU embeddings** with explicit model revisions and device selection.
- **Jupyter notebooks** for teaching, experiments, and visuals.
- A small shared Python package so notebooks, tests, and the eventual serving API use the same implementation.

**The curriculum should progress through six stages.**

| Stage | Coverage | What students demonstrate |
|---|---|---|
| Foundations | Vector geometry, similarity metrics, embeddings, tokenization, normalization, exact search, lexical search | Implement and explain a baseline without hiding the mechanics |
| Retrieval engineering | Qdrant data modeling, ingestion, chunking, metadata filters, HNSW, hybrid search, reranking | Improve retrieval quality against a fixed evaluation set |
| Applications | RAG, recommendations, deduplication, semantic caching, routing, agent memory, classification, multimodal search | Choose representations and metrics appropriate to each application |
| Advanced methods | Learned sparse retrieval, Matryoshka embeddings, late interaction, contextual retrieval, graph-assisted retrieval, visual document retrieval | Measure when added complexity helps |
| Production engineering | Serving, authorization, concurrency, freshness, migrations, observability, capacity, backups, replication | Operate the system and recover from failures |
| Capstone | An evaluated service with architectural decisions and operational exercises | Defend quality, latency, cost, and reliability tradeoffs with evidence |

The blueprint expands this into **30 proposed notebooks**, with a core path and optional application/research branches. I’d budget roughly **40–60 hours for the core**, plus additional time for advanced labs and the capstone, then revise those estimates after piloting.

**The most important additions to consider are these:**

1. **Teach evaluation before optimization.**  
   Introduce relevance judgments, Recall@k, MRR, and nDCG near the beginning. Distinguish “ANN found the same neighbors as exhaustive search” from “the retrieved documents answered the question.” Keep tuning queries separate from the final test set.

2. **Make ingestion and data lifecycle first-class topics.**  
   Include stable document/chunk IDs, provenance, retries, deduplication, updates, deletion, stale content, embedding versioning, and reindexing. Students should rebuild the index from retained source data and recover from an interrupted ingestion.

3. **Give non-RAG applications their own success criteria.**  
   Recommendation quality is different from retrieval relevance. Semantic caching needs false-hit tests. Entity matching needs false-merge analysis. Agent memory needs correction, expiration, and deletion behavior. These should be executable labs, not a list of potential use cases.

4. **Teach permissions as part of retrieval architecture.**  
   Tenant boundaries and document permissions must apply across candidate retrieval, reranking, caches, and returned evidence. Include negative tests where the system must return nothing, even when an unauthorized document is the closest semantic match.

5. **Include situations where vector search is the wrong choice.**  
   Compare against exact lookups, SQL predicates, lexical search, and simple exhaustive scans. Show identifier-heavy queries, small datasets, and transactional workloads where another approach may be simpler or more accurate.

6. **Make failures visible.**  
   Include negation, outdated instructions, contradictory documents, unanswerable questions, truncated inputs, poor chunk boundaries, revoked access, and malicious retrieved instructions. A useful exercise is: “The result looks plausible—find why it is wrong.”

7. **Separate retrieval quality from answer quality.**  
   RAG needs separate assessment of retrieved evidence, context assembly, answer correctness, citation support, and abstention. An LLM judge can assist, but should not be the only source of evaluation.

8. **Treat reproducibility as part of the lesson.**  
   Record dataset hashes, model revisions, settings, hardware, server/client versions, and warm/cold cache state. Every notebook should run from a fresh kernel and produce a readable static export.

For advanced coverage, I’d teach **established techniques plus a maintained research track**, rather than promise a permanently “most state-of-the-art” recipe. Qdrant’s documented multi-stage queries provide a practical basis for fusion and candidate rescoring. Matryoshka models and ColBERT-style late interaction introduce different quality/storage tradeoffs that students can investigate. [Qdrant multi-stage queries](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/hybrid-queries/), [Matryoshka research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13147), [ColBERTv2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01488).

The research track can extend to visual document retrieval and multi-vector compression. These should include small CPU experiments where feasible and explicitly labeled replay artifacts when the encoder is too expensive for a normal lesson. A small demonstration would teach the mechanism without claiming to reproduce the paper’s performance. [ColPali](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01449), [MUVERA](https://research.google/blog/muvera-making-multi-vector-retrieval-as-fast-as-single-vector-search/).

**Each notebook should follow a consistent teaching pattern:** an engineering question → intuition and necessary mathematics → a baseline → one controlled change → measured results and visuals → a failure case → an exercise → production implications. Useful visuals include ranking changes, similarity heatmaps, recall/latency curves, threshold precision/recall plots, and request traces. Two-dimensional embedding plots are useful illustrations, but should not stand in for retrieval evaluation.

Two practical decisions deserve explicit treatment:

- **CPU resource budgets.** Start with a small encoder, small reranker, and tiny/standard/scale dataset profiles. Measure batching, sequence length, threading, and optional ONNX inference. Keep model-weight quantization separate from stored-vector quantization. [Sentence Transformers CPU/backend guidance](https://www.sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/usage/efficiency.html).
- **The generation backend.** CPU embeddings do not determine how answers are generated. I recommend a core course that requires no paid API, with retrieval and context assembly fully executable locally, plus an explicit real-generation extension. Extractive displays or prerecorded answers must be labeled as such.

content.text:
**The direction is good, but I’d tighten five parts before treating this as the implementation specification.** The stack and overall architecture fit the goal. The main risks are misleading experiments, an incomplete RAG experience, and too much material packed into individual notebooks.

I reviewed the full blueprint and checked Qdrant’s indexing behavior against its documentation.

1. **High priority: make relevance judgments independent of chunking.**  
   The design compares chunking strategies, but it does not define how relevance labels survive changes to chunk boundaries. If labels attach to the original chunks, changing chunk size changes the evaluation target. Overlapping chunks can also inflate apparent success.

   **Fix:** anchor gold evidence to source document revisions and source spans. Define how retrieved chunks map to that evidence, deduplicate document-level results, and compare context quality under a fixed token budget as well as fixed `k`. Explicitly define metric handling for unanswerable queries and partially judged datasets.  
   See [evaluation data design](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md:121).

2. **High priority: ensure the ANN lab actually exercises an ANN index.**  
   The small datasets are sensible for teaching, but Qdrant does not automatically index every segment; optimizer settings and segment size matter, and filter cardinality influences query planning. Without an explicit setup check, students could vary HNSW parameters while effectively measuring scans and draw incorrect conclusions. [Qdrant indexing documentation](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/indexing/)

   **Fix:** give the ANN notebook a dedicated configuration and dataset profile. Verify index construction has completed, record indexing and scan thresholds, account for filter selectivity, and separate ingestion/index-building time from query benchmarks. An inconclusive parameter sweep should be reported as inconclusive.  
   See [the ANN lesson](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md:48).

3. **Medium priority: resolve the generation dependency across the core course.**  
   Generation is optional in notebook 12, but notebook 13 includes query rewriting, decomposition, contextual retrieval, and iterative retrieval. Those require either a real model, supplied transformations, or explicitly simplified implementations. As written, the default path could finish without executing an actual generative RAG system.

   **Fix:** define two explicit execution profiles: retrieval-only and live RAG. Make one small end-to-end live RAG exercise required for completing the RAG track, with a selected backend, resource limits, citations, and no-answer tests. Prewritten rewrites can teach retrieval mechanics, but should not count as executing model-driven rewriting.  
   See [RAG lessons 12–13](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md:51).

4. **Medium priority: turn the topic list into bounded lesson contracts.**  
   Several entries are effectively mini-courses: multilingual/code/multimodal retrieval; classification/clustering/anomaly detection; and recovery/replication/failure drills. The document allows splitting them later, but that leaves the actual scope and CPU feasibility open.

   **Fix:** define each lesson’s prerequisites, required experiment, expected outputs, runtime target, memory/download budget, and completion check. Split the overloaded lessons before authoring. Keep one primary engineering question per notebook, with extensions clearly separated. Select and pin the core models and dataset after the initial pilot, before expanding the course.  
   See [the notebook sequence](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md:35).

5. **Medium priority: give storage internals a dedicated learning outcome.**  
   The design is stronger on retrieval techniques than on explaining how a vector store behaves under changing data. WALs, segments, optimization, and storage overhead appear, but there is no focused lesson connecting them to write visibility, indexing lag, update/delete behavior, disk growth, and concurrent search.

   **Fix:** add a “life of a write” lesson between Qdrant basics and performance tuning. Trace ingestion through persistence and indexing, then measure searches during updates and deletions. Explain which observations are specific to Qdrant and which principles transfer to other systems.  
   See [Qdrant fundamentals](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md:44) and [production tradeoffs](/Users/markcastillo/git/vector-masterclass/docs/CURRICULUM.md:160).

The parts I would keep are **evaluation early, a real Compose server, notebooks backed by shared Python code, non-RAG applications, explicit failure exercises, and migration/restore testing**. Those give the course substance beyond a collection of API examples.

**I’d proceed with the first vertical-slice pilot**, incorporating the evaluation and ANN safeguards immediately. The remaining findings should be resolved before bulk notebook authoring. There is no architectural reason to change Qdrant, CPU embeddings, Python, uv, or Jupyter.

This was a design review only; I haven’t changed the files or validated runtime feasibility.

+def ranking_metrics(ranked: list[str], relevance: dict[str, int], k: int) -> dict:

+"""Inspectable chunk boundaries with character offsets into immutable canonical text."""
+
+import re
+
+from .schema import Chunk, Document

+def chunk_document(doc: Document, strategy: str = "fixed", words: int = 48, overlap: int = 8) -> list[Chunk]:
+    if words <= 0 or not 0 <= overlap < words:
+        raise ValueError("Require words > 0 and 0 <= overlap < words")
+    if strategy == "document":
+        return [Chunk.from_span(doc, 0, len(doc.text), "document")]
+    if strategy == "structural":
+        return [Chunk.from_span(doc, m.start(), m.end(), strategy) for m in re.finditer(r"[^\n]+(?:\n(?!\n)[^\n]+)*", doc.text)]
+    if strategy not in {"fixed", "parent_child"}:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown chunk strategy: {strategy}")
+    tokens = list(re.finditer(r"\S+", doc.text))
+    parent = Chunk.from_span(doc, 0, len(doc.text), "document")
+    chunks = []
+    for index in range(0, len(tokens), words - overlap):
+        group = tokens[index:index + words]
+        start, end = group[0].start(), group[-1].end()
+        chunks.append(Chunk.from_span(doc, start, end, f"{strategy}:{words}:{overlap}", parent.id if strategy == "parent_child" else None))
+        if index + words >= len(tokens):
+            break
+    return chunks
+
+
+def pack_chunks(chunks: list[Chunk], tokenizer, budget: int) -> dict:
+    """Whole-chunk greedy packing includes citation header tokens and separators."""
+    if budget <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("Context budget must be positive")
+    parts, selected, seen = [], [], set()
+    for chunk in chunks:
+        if chunk.id in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(chunk.id)
+        part = f"[{chunk.id}] {chunk.text}"
+        candidate = "\n\n".join([*parts, part])
+        count = len(tokenizer.encode(candidate, add_special_tokens=False))
+        if count <= budget:

+            selected.append(chunk)
+    text = "\n\n".join(parts)
+    return {"text": text, "chunks": selected, "tokens": len(tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)), "budget": budget}

+"""Transparent lexical, exhaustive, fusion, and diversity baselines."""
+
+import re
+
+import numpy as np
+from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi
+
+
+def tokenize(text: str) -> list[str]:
+    return re.findall(r"[\w]+(?:[-.]\w+)*", text.lower())
+
+
+def normalized(vectors: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    vectors = np.asarray(vectors, dtype=np.float32)
+    norms = np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
+    if not np.isfinite(vectors).all() or np.any(norms == 0):
+        raise ValueError("Vectors must be finite and nonzero")
+    return vectors / norms
+
+
+def exact_search(query: np.ndarray, vectors: np.ndarray, ids: list[str], k: int = 5) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
+    if k <= 0 or len(ids) != len(vectors) or len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
+        raise ValueError("Require positive k and unique IDs aligned with vectors")
+    if not ids:
+        return []
+    q = normalized(query)
+    matrix = normalized(vectors)
+    if matrix.ndim != 2 or q.ndim != 1 or matrix.shape[1] != q.shape[0]:
+        raise ValueError("Vector dimensions do not match")
+    scores = matrix @ q
+    # Stable explicit ID tie-break so reruns do not depend on ingestion order.
+    order = sorted(range(len(ids)), key=lambda i: (-float(scores[i]), ids[i]))[:k]
+    return [(ids[i], float(scores[i])) for i in order]
+
+
+class LexicalIndex:
+    def __init__(self, texts: list[str], ids: list[str]):
+        if not texts or len(texts) != len(ids) or len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
+            raise ValueError("Lexical index requires aligned nonempty texts and unique IDs")
+        self.ids = ids
+        self.index = BM25Okapi([tokenize(t) for t in texts])
+
+    def search(self, query: str, k: int = 5) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
+        if k <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("k must be positive")
+        scores = self.index.get_scores(tokenize(query))
+        order = sorted(range(len(self.ids)), key=lambda i: (-float(scores[i]), self.ids[i]))[:k]
+        return [(self.ids[i], float(scores[i])) for i in order]
+
+
+def reciprocal_rank_fusion(rankings: list[list[str]], constant: int = 60) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
+    """One-based ranks; duplicates within a retriever cannot earn repeated credit."""
+    if constant < 0:
+        raise ValueError("Fusion constant must be nonnegative")
+    scores = {}
+    for ranked in rankings:
+        for rank, id_ in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(ranked), 1):
+            scores[id_] = scores.get(id_, 0) + 1 / (constant + rank)
+    return sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))
+
+
+def mmr(query: np.ndarray, vectors: np.ndarray, k: int, weight: float = 0.7) -> list[int]:
+    if not 0 <= weight <= 1 or k <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("Require positive k and weight in [0, 1]")
+    if len(vectors) == 0:
+        return []
+    matrix, query = normalized(vectors), normalized(query)
+    relevance = matrix @ query
+    similarity = matrix @ matrix.T
+    selected, remaining = [], set(range(len(vectors)))
+    while remaining and len(selected) < k:
+        scores = {i: weight * relevance[i] - (1 - weight) * max((similarity[i, j] for j in selected), default=0) for i in remaining}
+        best = min(remaining, key=lambda i: (-float(scores[i]), i))
+        selected.append(best)
+        remaining.remove(best)
+    return selected

+These are local observations from M0, not production qualification. The user changed the scope during implementation to **macOS on Apple Silicon only**, with CPU and Metal GPU permitted when useful. That instruction supersedes the original CPU-only design and initial goal wording.
+
+## Runtime and isolation
+
+- Python 3.12.13, uv project and `uv.lock`; native macOS inference with PyTorch 2.15.0, Transformers 4.57.6, Sentence Transformers 5.7.0. The lockfile is the exact dependency record.
+- Qdrant server/client 1.17.1, server image pinned to digest `sha256:94728574965d17c6485dd361aa3c0818b325b9016dac5ea6afec7b4b2700865f`. Docker Compose publishes only loopback ports 6333/6334; persistence uses project-named volumes. The Qdrant container is capped at 6 GiB and four CPUs.
+- Observed host: Apple Silicon arm64 with 96 GiB unified memory. Docker engine 29.8.2, Compose 5.5.0. The 16 GiB course envelope is a design target; it has not been independently tested on a 16 GiB Mac.
+- Model inference stays native to access MPS. There is no CUDA/Linux learner-host support, automatic cloud inference, or implicit GPU-to-CPU fallback. `VMC_DEVICE` and `VMC_DEVICE_<MODEL_KEY>` make device overrides explicit. Requesting unavailable MPS fails.
+- CPU is the default for tiny dense/reranking/sparse exercises; GPU benefit depends on batch size. Lesson 20a measures the tradeoff rather than treating GPU as universally faster. Generation uses MPS/bfloat16 after the numerical and quality checks below.
+
+## Models and numerical precision
+
+All core models have Apache-2.0 model-card licenses and immutable revisions recorded in `configs/models.json`. `vmc bootstrap` copies existing matching snapshots or explicitly downloads the pinned files, hashes every retained file, and writes a local manifest. Inference loads local files only. Model-weight licenses remain separate from the course's source material.
+
+| Role | Model | Initial operating choice |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Dense embedding | sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 | CPU, 384 dimensions, normalized, 256-token limit, no role prefixes |
+| Reranker | cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 | CPU, 512-token query/document input limit |
+| Learned sparse | prithivida/Splade_PP_en_v1 | CPU masked-LM logits, max log1p-ReLU pooling, explicit top-128 nonzero pruning |
+| Generator | Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | Native MPS, bfloat16, greedy decoding, 2,048-token course context cap, at most 128 new tokens |
+
+The sparse pooling/pruning settings are part of the representation contract; this implementation is a bounded teaching configuration, not a reproduction of a published SPLADE benchmark.
+
+The initial 0.5B CPU generator produced a correct short warranty answer without the requested citation. Its no-answer response was semantically an abstention but did not match the exact requested phrase. The original exact-string check reported false; this is a lesson in separating format compliance from semantic correctness, not evidence of a hallucinated waterproof rating. Raw run: `artifacts/20261031T012532Z-a9d2a8/pilot/manifest.json`.
+
+The 1.5B float16/MPS trial produced repeated exclamation marks. It was rejected. The implementation now rejects nonfinite generation logits and uses bfloat16 explicitly. Raw rejected run: `artifacts/20261031T013121Z-bd575d/pilot/manifest.json`. Do not infer that all float16 models or all MPS configurations fail from this single observation.
+
+The bfloat16/MPS pilot passed the small factual-answer, citation-presence, and exact abstention-format checks. Whole-pilot execution after explicit bootstrap took about 6.2 seconds, with sampled process-tree RSS around 0.94 GiB and MPS driver allocation around 3.10 GiB. Those memory fields may overlap in unified memory; they must not be summed as if they are disjoint physical allocations. This two-question check establishes feasibility, not general answer quality. Raw run: `artifacts/20261031T013245Z-dbfa21/pilot/manifest.json`.
+
+Generation's `max_time` is a cooperative decoding limit, not hard process cancellation. Serving and iterative retrieval must additionally enforce their own request/call budgets and disclose non-cancellable work.
+
+## Qdrant schema and ANN validity
+
+The server rejected adding an unconfigured sparse-vector field through ordinary collection update. The collection must declare the sparse field at creation; migration code must respect the pinned schema. This observed API behavior is covered by the data-model lesson rather than hidden behind a fallback.
+
+The server also rejected `full_scan_threshold=0`, requiring at least 10. The ANN probe uses that supported minimum, 6,000 normalized random 64-dimensional vectors, HNSW m=8/ef_construct=40, indexing threshold 64, and a bounded wait for at least 99% indexed vectors. It compares server exact results with NumPy and approximate results with the exact oracle.
+
+In the twelve-query feasibility probe, mean ANN Recall@10 rose from about 0.28 at ef=8 to 0.88 at ef=128. Median HTTP search latency remained roughly 1.1–1.3 ms. This is synthetic index-fidelity evidence, not semantic relevance or a representative performance benchmark. There was no per-query execution trace; index coverage/configuration and observed fidelity differences support the interpretation, with that limitation disclosed. Raw run: `artifacts/20261031T013301Z-c5982e/ann_probe/manifest.json`.
+
+## Data and label decisions
+
+The fictional corpus contains 25 immutable source revisions and fourteen queries. Development gold sources use the Atlas family; test gold sources use Boreal. Controlled cases include obsolete firmware, negation, similar identifiers, private tenant data, and unsupported questions. Query evidence is anchored to canonical character offsets and source hashes. The user approved the listed gold labels; `configs/gold_review.json` binds that approval to corpus/query hashes. A changed file invalidates the approval automatically.
+
+The external benchmark is BEIR SciFact: full 5,183-document corpus, with the first twenty numeric query IDs from train for development and first twenty from test for evaluation. Selection was fixed before model scoring. Its CC-BY-SA-4.0 attribution and judgment limitations are in `datasets/README.md`; exact source/file hashes are in `configs/benchmark.json`. The original archive download was slow but completed; no alternate dataset was substituted.
+
+## Evidence interpretation and next gates
+
+M0 feasibility does not satisfy M1–M7. Each lesson still needs a real experiment, exercise/solution, fresh execution, result artifact, and visual review. M1's metric fixtures already cover document deduplication, graded ranking, no-answer exclusion, overlapping evidence spans, alternative evidence, immutable revision hashes, and explicit ties. Later stages add integration, serving, lifecycle, generation, and application checks.
+
+The pilot resource targets remain conservative authoring limits. Model and process measurements from a large-memory Mac do not establish behavior under actual 16 GiB host pressure. Advanced model downloads and multi-node runs require separately recorded budgets.

+# Worked solutions and instructor notes
+
+Read these after attempting the exercises. A correct result should be accompanied by an explanation of assumptions, a failure case, and a decision about when the technique is appropriate. Later milestone solutions will be added alongside their notebooks.
+
+## 00 — Environment and first retrieval
+
+The Docker service is a Linux process in a VM and does not expose the native Mac Metal backend to this Python process. Run Qdrant in Docker and model inference natively. A third warranty sentence should be judged on the query's product identity as well as topical similarity; inspect the returned payload rather than assuming the first hit is correct. Stopping Qdrant should yield a bounded readiness failure. Missing model files require the explicit bootstrap step.
+
+## 01 — Geometry
+
+For the replacement `[0.8, 0.1]`, dot product with `[1, 0]` is 0.8, cosine is approximately 0.9923, and Euclidean distance is approximately 0.2236. The exact-direction candidate `[1, 0]` still wins all three comparisons in this modified example. A zero vector has zero norm, making cosine division undefined. Normalization removes magnitude information; use it only when appropriate to the representation and metric. Plot equal axis scales if you interpret angles.
+
+## 02 — Embedding limitations
+
+Moving the warranty sentence before the filler puts it within the model's input window; placing it after enough filler removes it before inference. That is a tokenizer/input-budget effect, not a database failure. Similar identifiers and negated statements may remain close because much of their context is shared. Exact lexical matching or typed fields preserve codes; chunking preserves relevant text; reranking can improve relevance but still requires measurement. Do not use cosine similarity as factual equivalence.
+
+## 03 — Baselines
+
+An exact identifier query can favor BM25, while a paraphrase may favor dense retrieval. Inspect the development-case error involving E104: the Boreal document also mentions Atlas E104, making it a plausible distractor even though the labeled Atlas document is the intended primary source. This illustrates that a small gold set can omit partially useful results; the lesson reports supplied-label metrics, not perfect knowledge of all relevance. Expand or refine judgments through a new reviewed version rather than silently relabeling after inspecting test results.
+
+Neither retriever automatically abstains when there is no answer: both rank available documents. Retrieval thresholds require development calibration and no-answer tests. Keeping the test set unchanged prevents a demonstration from becoming a tuned anecdote.
+
+## 04 — Evaluation
+
+With ranks `noise, A, A, B`, deduplicate to `noise, A, B`. Recall@3 is 1, MRR is 1/2, and nDCG uses `(3/log2(3)+1/2)/(3+1/log2(3))`. For source intervals `[0,4)` and `[2,6)`, union length is 6, not 8. If full coverage is required, any uncovered character interval prevents that unit from passing. Alternative spans within one evidence unit are alternative supports for one fact; satisfying either is sufficient and does not double the denominator. No-answer recall is undefined, not zero; report false retrieval/abstention separately.
+
+## 05a — Data model
+
+Fresh random point IDs produce distinct points even for identical text. A deterministic UUID derived from source revision, canonical source hash, chunking configuration, and span makes a repeated ingestion idempotent. Changing the source/chunking intentionally changes IDs and requires removal of obsolete points. Tenant payloads require server-side access filtering and authoritative policy checks; storing a tenant field alone provides no access control. Dimension validation rejects structural mismatch but cannot detect semantically incompatible models with equal dimensions.

+"""Bounded context with request-local citations resolving to immutable source spans."""
+
+import re
+
+from .schema import Chunk, Document
+
+
+def validate_chunk(chunk: Chunk, sources: list[Document], tenant: str):
+    by_key = {(d.tenant, d.key): d for d in sources if d.active}
+    doc = by_key.get((chunk.tenant, chunk.document_key))
+    if chunk.tenant not in {"public", tenant} or doc is None:
+        raise PermissionError("Evidence is not in the authorized active source snapshot")
+    if (
+        chunk.source_hash != doc.sha256
+        or not 0 <= chunk.start < chunk.end <= len(doc.text)
+        or chunk.text != doc.text[chunk.start : chunk.end]
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Evidence text/hash/span does not match its canonical source")
+
+
+def assemble(chunks: list[Chunk], sources: list[Document], tokenizer, budget: int, *, tenant: str):
+    if budget <= 0 or not tenant:
+        raise ValueError("Require a positive token budget and an explicit tenant")
+    selected, parts, citations, seen = [], [], {}, set()
+    for chunk in chunks:
+        # Validate even duplicates/oversize chunks: reject poisoned inputs before packing.
+        validate_chunk(chunk, sources, tenant)
+        if chunk.id in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(chunk.id)
+        label = f"E{len(selected) + 1}"
+        candidate = "\n\n".join([*parts, f"[{label}] {chunk.text}"])
+        if len(tokenizer.encode(candidate, add_special_tokens=False)) > budget:
+            continue
+        selected.append(chunk)
+        parts.append(f"[{label}] {chunk.text}")
+        citations[label] = chunk.model_dump()
+    text = "\n\n".join(parts)
+    return {
+        "text": text,
+        "chunks": selected,
+        "citations": citations,
+        "tokens": len(tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)),
+        "budget": budget,
+    }
+
+
+def citation_audit(answer: str, citations: dict) -> dict:
+    """Check referential validity only; a resolvable citation need not support the claim."""
+    labels = list(dict.fromkeys(re.findall(r"\[(E\d+)\]", answer)))
+    return {
+        "labels": labels,
+        "unknown": [label for label in labels if label not in citations],
+        "has_citation": bool(labels),
+        "all_resolve": bool(labels) and all(label in citations for label in labels),
+    }

+## 06 — Retryable ingestion
+
+At an interruption after one source upsert, the remote store has changed and later events remain pending. Replay rewrites stable IDs and then completes the manifest. A zero boundary interrupts before any remote work; both paths should converge. Include tenant identity in IDs to prevent identical same-named documents in two tenants overwriting one another. +
+Compare evidence coverage and consumed tokens, not chunk recall alone. Overlapping spans earn their union length once. Parent expansion can restore qualifiers but may exceed a whole-chunk packing budget. Score claim correctness, procedure ordering, completeness, citation support, and abstention separately; see `RAG_RESULTS.md` for the full author review. +
+The reference planner invented AT&T and software version 2.3.5 and sometimes changed E104 to 104. Yet the tiny-corpus MRR stayed unchanged. Ranking success therefore does not validate transformation fidelity. An identifier validator can reject dropped/changed codes and added versions, but preserving those tokens does not prove the rewritten question has the same meaning. Retain the original query branch, bound calls, measure marginal evidence gain, and keep generated text outside the policy/authorization interface.
+
+## 13b — Contextual enrichment
+
+A generated prefix omitted the “accidental water” qualifier from “damage,” and another changed E104 to 104. Novel-token detection flags some changes but misses a false generalization built entirely from original words. Source-span checks pass because the original chunk is intact; they cannot establish annotation truth. Review annotations or use a task-specific supported-fact validator, and measure whether enrichment actually helps. On the reference six-document development slice, both representations had equal evidence coverage, so the extra preprocessing cost had no observed retrieval benefit.

+
+Both answerable two-fact scenarios already had their source targets after the initial search. The loop spent calls and stopped on a repeated query without improving coverage. The waterproof rating remained unsupported. A practical stopping rule can combine new unique evidence, unchanged candidate sets, a strict iteration/call/time cap, and an explicit unresolved-facts record. A model-generated STOP is advice, not proof of completeness. If partial answers are allowed, identify the missing part rather than guessing it.
+
+## 24 — Service boundary
+
+Payload tenant equality misses document-grant revocation within the same tenant. The fixture maps a known token to a server-owned identity, filters current authorized source revisions, validates returned spans, keys caches by policy/source epoch, and rechecks that epoch before responding. The timeout test keeps the native worker blocked after the 504 and verifies another request gets 429. Releasing the slot at response timeout would permit replacement work to accumulate. A separate process can support hard termination at additional model-loading and IPC cost. +import numpy as np

+def binary_metrics(expected, predicted):
+    expected,predicted = np.asarray(expected,dtype=bool),np.asarray(predicted,dtype=bool)
+    if expected.shape!=predicted.shape or expected.ndim!=1 or not len(expected):
+        raise ValueError('Require aligned nonempty one-dimensional binary labels')
+    tp = int((expected & predicted).sum())
+    fp = int((~expected & predicted).sum())
+    fn = int((expected & ~predicted).sum())
+    tn = int((~expected & ~predicted).sum())
+    return {'tp':tp,'fp':fp,'fn':fn,'tn':tn,'precision':tp/(tp+fp) if tp+fp else 0.,'recall':tp/(tp+fn) if tp+fn else 0.,'f1':2*tp/(2*tp+fp+fn) if 2*tp+fp+fn else 0.}
+
+
+def route(vector, prototypes, labels, *, threshold=.55, margin=.05):
+    if len(labels)!=len(prototypes) or len(set(labels))<2:
+        raise ValueError('Routing requires aligned prototypes for at least two intents')
+    scores = normalized(prototypes)@normalized(vector)
+    per_label = {label:max(float(s) for l,s in zip(labels,scores,strict=True) if l==label) for label in set(labels)}
+    ranked = sorted(per_label,key=lambda label:(-per_label[label],label))
+    best,second = ranked[:2]
+    accepted = per_label[best]>=threshold and per_label[best]-per_label[second]>=margin
+    return {'intent':best if accepted else 'abstain','best_intent':best,'score':per_label[best],'margin':per_label[best]-per_label[second],'authorized':False}

+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def clip_model(device):
+    from transformers import CLIPModel,CLIPProcessor
+    cpu_setup()
+    path = str(model_path('clip'))
+    return CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(path,local_files_only=True),CLIPModel.from_pretrained(path,local_files_only=True).to(device).eval()
+

+def clip_encode(*,texts=None,images=None,device=None):
+    if (texts is None)==(images is None):
+        raise ValueError('Encode either texts or images per call')
+    torch = cpu_setup()
+    selected = resolve_device('clip',device)
+    processor,model = clip_model(selected)
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        if texts is not None:
+            inputs = processor(text=texts,return_tensors='pt',padding=True,truncation=True,max_length=77).to(selected)
+            result = model.get_text_features(**inputs)
+        else:
+            inputs = processor(images=images,return_tensors='pt').to(selected)
+            result = model.get_image_features(**inputs)
+        result = torch.nn.functional.normalize(result,dim=-1)
+    synchronize(selected)
+    values = result.cpu().numpy()
+    if values.ndim!=2 or values.shape[1]!=model_config('clip')['dimensions'] or not np.isfinite(values).all():
+        raise ValueError('CLIP projection violated its representation contract')
+    return values

+"""Ordered source change log for a single-writer migration teaching exercise.
+
+Opaque source revisions are compared with CAS, not lexicographically ordered.
+The global sequence supplies replay order. Qdrant and SQLite are not atomic.
+"""
+
+import sqlite3
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from .schema import Document
+
+
+class SourceJournal:
+    def __init__(self, path: Path):
+        self.db = sqlite3.connect(path)
+        self.db.executescript("""
+          PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
+          CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS changes(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, source_json TEXT NOT NULL);
+          CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS current(tenant TEXT NOT NULL, source_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_json TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(tenant,source_id));
+          CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS consumers(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, pipeline TEXT NOT NULL, sequence INTEGER NOT NULL);
+        """)
+
+    def append(self, doc: Document, *, expected_revision: str | None):
+        with self.db:
+            row = self.db.execute("SELECT source_json FROM current WHERE tenant=? AND source_id=?", (doc.tenant,doc.id)).fetchone()
+            prior = Document.model_validate_json(row[0]) if row else None
+            if (prior.revision if prior else None) != expected_revision:
+                raise ValueError("Source revision conflict; stale writer rejected")
+            if prior and prior.revision == doc.revision:
+                raise ValueError("Each source event requires a new immutable revision")
+            sequence = self.db.execute("INSERT INTO changes(source_json) VALUES (?)", (doc.model_dump_json(),)).lastrowid
+            self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO current VALUES (?,?,?)", (doc.tenant,doc.id,doc.model_dump_json()))
+        return sequence
+
+    def snapshot(self):
+        # One read transaction; the course has one authoritative writer.
+        with self.db:
+            self.db.execute("BEGIN")
+            head = self.db.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sequence),0) FROM changes").fetchone()[0]
+            docs = [Document.model_validate_json(row[0]) for row in self.db.execute("SELECT source_json FROM current ORDER BY tenant,source_id")]
+        return head, docs
+
+    def cursor(self, ingestor):
+        row = self.db.execute("SELECT pipeline,sequence FROM consumers WHERE name=?", (ingestor.index.name,)).fetchone()
+        if row and row[0] != ingestor.pipeline_signature:
+            raise ValueError("Consumer pipeline changed; create another index")
+        return row[1] if row else 0
+
+    def replay(self, ingestor, *, stop_after=None, fail_before_checkpoint=False):
+        cursor = self.cursor(ingestor)
+        events = self.db.execute("SELECT sequence,source_json FROM changes WHERE sequence>? ORDER BY sequence", (cursor,)).fetchall()
+        count = 0
+        for sequence, payload in events:
+            if sequence != cursor + 1:
+                raise ValueError("Journal gap; cannot certify complete replay")
+            doc = Document.model_validate_json(payload)
+            if doc.active:
+                ingestor.ingest([doc])
+            else:
+                ingestor.delete(doc.id,doc.tenant)
+            if fail_before_checkpoint:
+                raise InterruptedError("Applied index update before journal cursor commit")
+            with self.db:
+                self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO consumers VALUES (?,?,?)", (ingestor.index.name,ingestor.pipeline_signature,sequence))
+            cursor = sequence
+            count += 1
+            if stop_after is not None and count >= stop_after:
+                break
+        return count
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.db.close()

+"""Context-managed loopback HTTP server for local integration/load exercises."""
+
+import socket
+import threading
+import time
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+import uvicorn
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def local_server(app):
+    sock=socket.socket()
+    sock.bind(('127.0.0.1',0))
+    sock.listen(128)
+    port=sock.getsockname()[1]
+    server=uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app,host='127.0.0.1',port=port,log_level='error',access_log=False))
+    worker=threading.Thread(target=server.run,kwargs={'sockets':[sock]},daemon=True)
+    worker.start()
+    try:
+        deadline=time.monotonic()+10
+        while not server.started:
+            if not worker.is_alive() or time.monotonic()>deadline:
+                raise RuntimeError('Local HTTP server failed to start')
+            time.sleep(.01)
+        yield f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}'
+    finally:
+        server.should_exit=True
+        worker.join(timeout=25)
+        sock.close()
+        if worker.is_alive():
+            raise RuntimeError('Local HTTP server did not shut down within 25 seconds')

content.text: The advanced lessons will distinguish real local experiments from research reproductions. They include trained Matryoshka embeddings and ColBERT token vectors, plus bounded visual-document and graph experiments. Quality regressions stay visible in the teaching material; passing a notebook means the experiment ran correctly, not that the advanced method won.

+# Architecture and worked design defense
+
+The reference system serves source-grounded retrieval with explicit revision, tenant, and representation contracts. The course is a laboratory for deciding what a real product needs; the local identity fixture, SQLite single-writer journal, tiny datasets, and one Docker host are deliberate boundaries.
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+  S[Canonical source revisions] --> J[Ordered change journal]
+  J --> I[Idempotent ingestion + checkpoints]
+  I --> E[Native CPU or MPS encoder]
+  E --> Q[Qdrant in Docker]
+  U[Validated request] --> P[Authoritative identity and policy]
+  P --> R[Bounded retrieval worker]
+  R --> Q
+  Q --> V[Source hash + span validation]
+  V --> C[Token-bounded cited evidence]
+  C --> G[Optional native generator]
+  P --> V
+  I --> M[External ingestion manifest]
+  J --> B[Recovery bundle + replay]
+  Q --> B
+```
+
+## Start with contracts
+
+The canonical document key is an ID plus opaque revision, qualified by tenant. Revisions are immutable: changed text requires another revision. Source spans use character offsets and a SHA-256 hash, defined before chunking. A chunk ID includes its source and representation. This lets evaluation survive chunker changes and makes retries converge. An ordered source journal supplies change order; sorting revision strings does not.
+
+An embedding contract includes model repository/revision, tokenizer limits, query/document roles and prefixes, normalization, dimensions, and representation strategy. Equal dimensions do not imply compatible spaces. Qdrant collection metadata verifies this contract before queries and writes. A model upgrade needs a versioned collection and a matching query encoder. Device choice is recorded but is not a new semantic space when measured numerical drift is acceptable.
+
+The source journal and current policy are authoritative. Qdrant is a derived retrieval index. A current policy check may exclude a deleted or revoked source before asynchronous physical cleanup. Durable deletion must also cover replicas, backups, caches, logs, and external manifests under a defined retention policy. The course demonstrates bounded logical deletion and replay, not secure erasure of all historical bytes.
+
+## Retrieval choices and their evidence
+
+| Requirement | Starting design | Evidence that can justify more complexity |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Exact identifiers, structured facts | SQL/key lookup or lexical search | Measured paraphrase failures justify dense retrieval. |
+| Semantic passage search | Small normalized dense encoder with exact reference search | A sufficiently large corpus and measured latency justify HNSW. |
+| Mixed identifier and paraphrase queries | Lexical/dense rank fusion | Evaluate candidate recall, held-out relevance, and added inference cost. |
+| Fine candidate distinctions | Cross-encoder or token MaxSim rescoring | Candidates must contain relevant sources; rerankers can regress. |
+| Large vector footprint | Width/quantization/on-disk experiments | Measure fidelity and semantic quality separately, actual disk/memory, build costs, and latency under pressure. |
+| Relationship queries | Structured lookup or provenance-backed graph | Graph traversal helps only with valid entities/edges and bounded expansion. |
+| Visual pages | Text baseline plus image/page retrieval | Layout, tables, small text, languages, and source-grounded evidence extraction need dedicated judgments. |
+| Answers rather than documents | Bounded context plus real local generator | Separate retrieval coverage, claim correctness, citation support, and abstention. |
+
+The reference SciFact comparison includes a reranker regression. Tiny routing fixtures can yield zero accepted requests at a conservative development threshold. Full context can still produce contradictory reset advice, false abstention, or incorrect citations. +
+## Serving and access
+
+The local API accepts a query and retrieval mode, never a caller-supplied tenant or arbitrary filter. Known demonstration tokens resolve to server-owned identities. Current authorized document revisions constrain every dense, sparse, and hybrid branch. Returned text must match canonical spans. Cache keys include identity, tenant, policy/source epoch, representation, collection, and query. Policy is checked around work and before responding.

+A production identity adapter must validate an issuer/audience, signature, expiry, and revocation policy with a real provider; demo tokens do not implement this. A revocation after the final check can race with network delivery; define the consistency/latency requirement rather than promise cross-store atomic authorization.
+
+The worker pool bounds native computation. Request timeout does not terminate a running Python/native model task; its slot remains occupied until actual completion. Overload returns 429 and bounded clients retry within an overall budget. Process isolation can provide stronger cancellation at the cost of model duplication, IPC, and restart latency. The local API serves retrieval; notebook generation is not a deployed generation service.
+

+
+Backfill a new representation from a source snapshot at a known journal watermark. Replay ordered changes and tombstones to both old and new indexes, persist each consumer checkpoint only after remote writes complete, and reconcile source mappings. A repeated event must converge after a crash between remote write and checkpoint. Cut over only when the target is caught up, the query encoder contract matches, and policy is current. The demonstration drains/recreates the service around Qdrant alias changes; alias atomicity alone does not update application encoders or policies.
+
+Keep the old index consuming changes for a bounded rollback window. Rolling back the application must not restore old permissions or resurrect deleted content. Account for dual storage, duplicate encoding, journal retention, and operational staffing.
+
+A recovery bundle needs Qdrant snapshots, ingestion manifests, current or replayable source state, policy history/current policy, model/configuration artifacts, aliases, and checksums. Restore into a clean target, verify point IDs/payloads/vectors, replay subsequent changes, reconcile, then reopen serving after current-policy tests. The local RTO begins at snapshot upload and excludes detection, host provisioning, and remote download. Its RPO measures missing retained journal events, not source events that were never durably captured.

+
+Before deploying, replace fictional task labels with a human-reviewed representative holdout, including languages, source families, time ranges, no-answer cases, and adverse slices. Define numeric SLO/RTO/RPO and error budgets before experiments, then exercise saturation, dependency failure, corruption, stale policy, and recovery.

+Three containers on one Mac share power, storage, VM, and host failure. Independent-host replication, network partitions, rolling upgrades, backups outside the failure domain, capacity under degraded replicas, and incident operations remain unqualified. +# Instructor runbook

+uv run pytest -q
+uv run python scripts/check_notebooks.py
